## Summary

**LOADI** (Load Indirect source into register): Load 64 bit indirect into destination register.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `<vea> → (d)` |
| Syntax | `LOADI <vea>,d` |
| Short | Load 64 bit indirect into destination register |
| Description | Loadi is the indexed variant of load. For many cases, the normal store instruction is more appropriate and convenient. While this indexed variant requires to preload the index register, it helps for example at places where the source register is to be changed conditionally. Also, you may think of storing a list of AMMX registers in a loop instead of in a row to keep code size small (where appropriate). |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | `0` |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | `0001` |
| 2 | 11–8 | d |
| 2 | 7–0 | `00000001` |

- (d) value → register

```text
  00 - 07 = D0  -  D7
  08 - 15 = A0  -  A7
  16 - 23 = B0  -  B7
  40 - 47 = E0  -  E7
  48 - 55 = E8  -  E15
  56 - 63 = E16 - E23
```

### Example

- if d1=47 then

```asm
    loadi (a0),d1
```

- would do the same as

```asm
    load (a0),e7
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no LOADI. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- No rules beyond the details above.
